steps.content: A warped haze of light floods your vision, forcing you to squint. It takes a moment before the scene at the center comes into focus.
Not far ahead, a long, crumbling staircase of the void is flaking away, inch by inch. At the top of the stairs stands a familiar silhouette.
You rush forward, but the silhouette retreats into the mist, leaving nothing but a trail of feathers behind.
You look toward where Phanuel vanished. The crumbling steps stretch upward in broken fragments, reaching into the sky.
[Water Dripping Sound Effect] [Scene Change: Home]
The scene before you shatters into pixels, fractures, and reassembles into an unfamiliar living room. It's lavishly decorated, clearly worth a fortune. Yet, there's no sign of Phanuel anywhere.
Daddy, look! My teacher said I did a really good job today and gave me this little red flower sticker!
steps.female_content: Mommy, look! My teacher said I did a really good job today and gave me this little red flower sticker!

steps.content: You follow the sound and look down to find a doll at your feet.
"Daddy?" Is it talking... to you?

options: Ignore the doll and keep looking for Phanuel

steps.content: But the doll grabs the hem of your pants just like a child would.
Its eyeless face tilts up toward you, desperate for your praise.

steps.speaker: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.content: Good job. My child deserves nothing but the finest honors. Do you know why your teacher praised you?
Your voice comes out cold, the voice of a middle-aged man.
steps.female_content: Your voice comes out cold, the voice of a middle-aged woman.

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: Because I made the best work in the class! I'm more amazing than all of the other kids!

steps.speaker: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.content: Wrong!
Your tone suddenly turns stern, your grip on the doll tightening.

steps.speaker: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.content: Your teacher praised you because you are my child. Everything you wear is custom-made designer wear. You ride to kindergarten in a luxury car. When your teacher came for a home visit, she saw that you live in the most prestigious neighborhood in all of Eastside.

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: Designer wear? What's that? Is it something really, really good? Does that mean Daddy and Mommy love me a lot?
The little cotton head sways proudly from side to side. Your hand, which was reaching out to pat her head, stops.

steps.speaker: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.content: Love? That's for people without money. What we give you is worth far more than that. Designer brands are status and prestige. They make everyone look up to you.

steps.speaker: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.content: You are our child. You represent our name, so you cannot let anyone look down on you.
The little cotton head nods solemnly and earnestly. You try to end this conversation to no avail.

steps.speaker: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.content: What you want doesn't matter. Instead, observe what others have. Then, you take it. Once all the money, power, dignity, and security in the world are yours, all of those cheap things you've ever wanted will also be well within reach.

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: Okay! I understand now! ███ is Daddy and Mommy's pride! Higher, lift me higher!
You cannot make out her original name.
The doll laughs cheerfully as it's tossed up into the air—

You wrench free from the body that was controlling you. But just as your fingers are about to close around it, the doll grazes your fingertips and crashes to the ground, twisting into a warped plastic figure.
[Water droplet sound effect] [Scene Change: Hospital, Barbie Doll]

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: Are these people in the photo my parents? Did they lie to a lot of people and take their money?

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: No. Everything's all fuzzy. I just know there were a lot of people in uniforms, and some yellow tape. Then I got scared and fell from somewhere—

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: When I woke up, I saw more and more people holding microphones and cameras. They kept asking me questions.

steps.speaker: Doll
steps.content: Hmm? You don't know what you asked me, sir?
steps.female_content: Hmm? You don't know what you asked me, ma'am?

steps.content: The doll's warped head snaps toward you with a click, and with that, you lose control of your voice once more.

options: Come on, look at the camera and smile

steps.content: What a heartless little thing. Her parents have been locked up, and she's still smiling... Heh, gotta thank those two wretches for giving birth to such a pretty face though. The daughter of two devils with an angel's face... Ooh, I can practically smell the clicks!
Heck, some might just straight up forgive her after seeing that cute, pitiful little face. People do tend to let their hearts do the thinking, after all...
What you have witnessed may not be the whole truth, but it is what Phanuel remembers, nevertheless.
She listens to their remarks, constantly adjusting the curve of her smile to show them exactly what they want to see.
[Water droplet sound effect] [Scene Change: Hospital, Mannequin]

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Hi everyone, I'm Phanuel, an idol in training. Please support me.
This won't do. You're supposed to be an angel, got it? No one's going to adore someone this stiff!
You instantly recognize who you're playing as. It's Eliza.

options: Do you want to go back to living in the shadows?

steps.content: I can always just wipe your past clean before sending you out there again.

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: I don't want that... Phanuel is an angel.
The mannequin shifts its pose, tilting the wings on its back higher, displaying them more prominently.

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Higher! Fly higher!
She hovers just above the ground, cycling through one pose after another, all meant to please. The false sunlight of the illusion falls over her, casting a halo of sanctity.
You can sense that you haven't quite reached the heart of the Mania disaster yet. One final staircase stands between you and the true end of this paradise.
[Scene Change: D2 Streets, No Filter] [City Traffic White Noise]

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Ah, there you are! I knew you wouldn't just leave me behind.

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: You know, there are so many people out here! Phanuel almost got recognized!

options: Do you want to be recognized?

steps.content: This time, it's the real you. The bustling street forks beneath a massive Phanuel billboard—to the left, the concert venue; to the right, the alley where the two of you once shared ice cream.
She holds your hand, rising onto her tiptoes again and again with anticipation, waiting for you to take her somewhere new.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If what lies ahead is the end of this paradise, then I can't go there with you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The freedom I want you to see is the possibility beyond the stage, the freedom to choose. But if I make that choice for you, if I define your worth the same way everyone else in your past has...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And I'll be taking away your will, just like those people have.

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Then take it away!

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Please...

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: I've lived my whole life being told what to do, being defined by others. I'm used to it. So why won't you choose for me this time? After taking from me for all these years, why make me choose for myself now, of all times?!

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Why did you make me into an angel?

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Angels aren't gods. They're the same as other worshippers, only with wings. A prettier tool!

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Why... why show me the paradise you painted, if you'll only leave me stranded here?

steps.speaker: Phanuel
steps.content: Liar... Liar, liar, LIAR!
Faces layer upon faces, past and present, until at last they converge into the true Phanuel. A Phanuel shaped by a distorted past.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm sorry, Phanuel. I failed to teach you the most important lesson. I never got around to telling you what true happiness really is.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Happiness is built on what's real. It's because the training to become a true idol is grueling that ice cream tastes all the sweeter. It's because everyday life is full of troubles that Phanuel's smile becomes the remedy people need.
You walk toward her. The shackles extend from your palm, the dim, crimson glow surrounding her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm sorry. It never occurred to me that just because you're the angel meant to bring happiness to everyone, it doesn't mean you know what true happiness is.
There's no time to teach her more now. But the least you can do is help her tear away the illusion she's been hiding behind.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Happiness is like cuteness. There's no single answer. It can be imperfect, unconditional, priceless... the same goes for the people who find it.
